items.definition:
chemical compound used as anesthetic
Chloroform was once used as an anesthetic during surgery.

a follower of Confucius; relating to Confucius
Confucian philosophy emphasizes morality and ethics.

a shaft that converts reciprocating motion into rotary motion
The engine's crankshaft was damaged and needed replacement.

the action of fixing the boundary or limits of something
There was a clear demarcation line between the two territories.

the process of removing salt from seawater
Desalination plants are becoming more common in arid regions.

the ability to judge well
She showed great discernment in her choice of friends.

a right to cross or otherwise use someone else's land for a specified purpose
The property had an easement allowing the neighbor access to the lake.

a hormone that interacts with receptors in the brain to reduce pain
Exercise can release endorphins, leading to a feeling of well-being.

a broad horizontal band of sculpted or painted decoration
The ancient temple had an elaborate frieze depicting mythological scenes.

an animated anthropomorphic being in Jewish folklore
In the legend, the rabbi created a golem to protect the Jewish community.

inability to do something or to function normally
The illness led to his temporary incapacity to work.

the act of entering; a place or means of entry
The building's main ingress was blocked by construction.

a person suffering from leprosy; an outcast
Historically, lepers were often isolated from society.

a public outdoor swimming pool or beach resort
We spent the afternoon relaxing at the lido.

alfalfa (a plant grown for fodder)
Lucerne is a valuable forage crop for livestock.

the quality of being magnificent or splendid
The magnificence of the cathedral left them speechless.

marten (a type of mammal)
The marten is a slender, agile mammal related to weasels.

minstrel (a medieval singer or musician)
In medieval times, a minstrel would travel from court to court, entertaining nobles.

naturalism (a style of art or literature that shows things as they are in real life)
The artist's work was praised for its stark naturalism.

osmosis (process of gradual absorption, especially of knowledge or ideas)
He learned a lot about the business through osmosis, just by being around experienced colleagues.

outcrop (a rock formation that is visible on the surface)
Geologists studied the rock outcrop to understand the area's geological history.

the study of fossils
She decided to major in paleontology because of her interest in dinosaurs.

a particular way of speaking or using words, especially a way common to those with a particular job or interest
In legal parlance, "habeas corpus" refers to a specific writ.

a way, especially one of several possible variations, in which a set or number of things can be ordered or arranged
There are six possible permutations of the letters A, B, and C.

a network of nerves or vessels in the body
The solar plexus is a complex network of nerves in the abdomen.

the house of a Catholic priest; a body of presbyters
The priest lives in the presbytery next to the church.

the state or quality of conforming to conventionally accepted standards of behavior or morals
He was known for his strict adherence to social propriety.

the action or process of making someone or something look or feel younger, fresher, or more lively
The city park underwent a complete rejuvenation project.

a stone coffin, typically adorned with a sculpture or inscription and associated with the ancient Egyptians, Greeks, and Romans
The ancient sarcophagus was discovered in the tomb.

divine feminine creative power in Hinduism
In Hinduism, Shakti represents the dynamic energy of the universe.

a large number of similar things or events appearing or occurring in quick succession
There has been a recent spate of burglaries in the neighborhood.

the sideways and downward movement of the edge of a plate of the earth's crust into the mantle beneath another plate
The process of subduction creates deep ocean trenches.

a radioactive metallic element
Thorium is being explored as an alternative nuclear fuel.

a strong spasm or pang of pain
The country was in the throes of a major economic crisis.

growth or increase by gradual accumulation
The island grew through the accretion of sand and sediment.

kindness; generosity
His benevolence towards the poor was well-known.

a person or institution that owns bonds
The company reassured its bondholders about the financial stability.

a large, coarse fern
The hillside was covered in dense bracken.

a place where dead bodies are cremated
The funeral service was held at the local crematorium.

the process of removing dangerous substances
The area required full decontamination after the chemical spill.

A unit of fineness for yarn; a person who denies.
The fabric was made of 200 denier nylon.

a body of inspectors
The government inspectorate conducted a thorough review of the factory's safety standards.

any of several veins in the neck that drain blood from the head
The doctor checked the pulse in his jugular vein.

a thing used for tying or binding something tightly; a character consisting of two or more letters joined together
The surgeon applied a ligature to the bleeding vessel.

the belief or desire of a government or people that a country should maintain a strong military capability and be prepared to use it aggressively to defend or promote national interests.
The rise of militarism in the region led to increased tensions.

a medical practitioner qualified to diagnose and treat tumors.
The patient was referred to an oncologist for further evaluation.

a solution or remedy for all difficulties or diseases.
There is no single panacea for all of society's problems.

a very poor person.
He died a pauper, with no possessions to his name.

a machine designed to detect and record changes in physiological characteristics, such as a person's pulse and breathing rates, used especially as a lie detector.
The suspect was asked to take a polygraph test.

surrealism (art movement)
Salvador Dalí is a famous artist associated with surrealism.

a person who wanders from place to place
He lived the life of a vagabond, traveling wherever the road took him.

A trace or remnant
The old building was the last vestige of the ancient civilization.

The act of creating a virtual version of something
Cloud computing relies heavily on virtualization technology.

A person's face or facial expression
His stern visage showed no emotion.

A castrated ram
The farmer had several wethers in the flock.

The removal of a body part or tissue, or the erosion of material
The doctor performed a cardiac ablation to correct the arrhythmia.

A component of a machine that is responsible for moving or controlling a mechanism or system
The robot's arm uses a powerful actuator for precise movements.

Agriculture conducted on commercial principles, especially using advanced technology
Large corporations dominate the agribusiness sector.

In a frenzied or uncontrolled state
The crowd ran amok after the concert.

chest pain due to reduced blood flow to the heart
The patient experienced severe angina, indicating a heart problem.

a person attached to an embassy or consulate
The cultural attaché organized an exhibition of local art.

a tool for boring holes
He used an auger to drill holes for the fence posts.

a statement of the beliefs or aims that guide someone's actions
His personal credo was to always act with integrity.

the material or protoplasm within a living cell, excluding the nucleus
The cytoplasm contains various organelles essential for cell function.
